concept: Foundation of the Indian National Congress
question: Who is most commonly associated with the 'safety valve' theory regarding the formation of the Indian National Congress?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**AO Hume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Safety Valve Theory'** is associated with **AO Hume**, a retired British civil servant who played a key role in the formation of the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in 1885.
 
• This theory suggests that the British government supported the establishment of the INC as a means to provide a platform for Indians to express their grievances peacefully, thus preventing revolutionary activities.
 
• **AO Hume** believed that by channeling Indian discontent into constitutional and non-violent methods, the British could maintain control over India while addressing some concerns.
 
• He was instrumental in bringing together prominent Indian leaders and intellectuals to form the INC, which later became a significant force in India's struggle for independence.
 
• The INC was initially meant to serve as a forum for educated Indians to discuss political issues and advise the British administration on reforms.
 
• The theory has been debated by historians, with some accepting its validity and others arguing that the INC was formed due to genuine political aspirations of Indian leaders rather than British motives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Dufferin**__

 __
 
• **Lord Dufferin** was the **Viceroy of India** from 1884 to 1888.
 
• Although he did not directly form the INC, he interacted with its leaders and played a role in facilitating its early discussions.
 
• He supported the idea of addressing Indian grievances, but his involvement was more indirect compared to AO Hume.
 
 
 
• **WC Bannerji**__
 __
 
• **WC Bannerji** was the first president of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885.
 
• He was a prominent lawyer and political leader known for his advocacy of constitutional reforms and moderate politics.
 
• While he played an important role in the INC's early leadership, the 'Safety Valve Theory' is not directly associated with him.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**__
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was a key figure in Indian nationalism and the INC, often referred to as the **Grand Old Man of India**.
 
• He was known for his economic critique of British colonial rule, especially the **'Drain of Wealth' theory.**
 
• Though he contributed significantly to the INC, his focus was more on economic issues rather than the 'Safety Valve Theory.'
